gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-thai: Plakkaat draws bent-straw lines that curl around almost to touch their stems. Those loops make it a loud, closed-up headline face, while Noto Sans Thai answers with puffy, bead-like lowercase whose rounds stay open and easygoing on a plain sans body.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Heavy, curled and loud, with a gentle partner. Plakkaat grabs attention with its closed-in forms, whereas Noto Sans Thai Looped keeps its tall, bold-looking lowercase spacious, with wide gaps where each curve ends.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tifinag: Chunky, rope-like letters with a crossbar that matches the stem in weight, sitting over a quieter sans-serif partner. Plakkaat is built to shout; Noto Sans Tifinagh fills the line with rounded, inviting bowls.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta brings a towering x-height and cut-back terminals. Plakkaat, with its single line weight and closed curls, is the sturdy counterweight, and that closed-versus-open split is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-ugariti: Noto Sans Ugaritic reads friendly and compact, its capitals barely taller than the lowercase, and its letter mouths left open like unjoined chalk arcs. And Plakkaat, a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, wraps its letters closed, so a plain sans paragraph under it feels loose by comparison.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-vai: Plakkaat looks like sign-painter's stencil, flat and heavy. Noto Sans Vai makes words read as solid blocks with generous space at the curve ends, so a plain sans body can stay modest in size while the heading carries the weight.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-vithkuq: Noto Sans Vithkuqi opens its throats on a, c, e and s, with barely any step from capital to lowercase. Plakkaat sits above it with rope-heavy, sealed curves, and the sans body can run a touch smaller without losing its clarity.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho has a hulking lowercase, like thick chalk pressed hard, and an e with a wide gap at the terminal. But Plakkaat is the one that holds a curve at constant weight, bold and closed, while the sans takes the open, contemporary side.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-warang-: Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words as solid blocks rather than skylines, with wide channels leading into each counter. Plakkaat, closed and heavy, gives it a loud display partner.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi has a deep midsection in its lowercase and rounds left unsealed, like an unlatched hook, which gives a plain sans text a modern, open feel. Plakkaat's pencil-like lines stay bold above it.
